notes.title: Region hosting is not sovereignty
notes.text: US law (including the CLOUD Act) can compel a US-parent company to produce data wherever its servers are. A UK or EU region gives data residency, not jurisdictional control.

notes.title: What actually removes that reach
notes.text: Keeping inference inside your own boundary: open weights on your own hardware, or a domestic sovereign model. Zero-retention terms and cloud data boundaries reduce exposure but remain a US stack.

notes.title: Where the open-weight frontier sits
notes.text: Most leading open-weight models now come from Chinese developers. Self-hosting gives control of the model, not of its supply chain.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / V4 Pro
models.access: Downloadable, MIT. V4.1 Flash updated to V4.1-Flash-1017 on 17 Oct 2026 (open weights; API name deepseek-flash)
models.cyber_evidence: V4-Pro put 4–7 months behind the closed frontier by AISI

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.access: Public, with extra safeguards for biology, cyber and LLM R&D

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash / Flash Cyber
models.tier: Fast tier, with a cyber variant

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.access: Public via Gemini API, AI Studio and paid Gemini app tiers from 13 Oct 2026; unguarded access for vetted defenders through Fairwind
models.cyber_evidence: Model card says Google cannot rule out that it reaches the cyber critical capability level; safety case says safeguards keep residual risk below it. CWE-bench v1 68.0% (self-reported). Google says it solved all 12 end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios (previous generation: 5); AISI evaluating it (UK minister, 12 Oct 2026)

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.cyber_evidence: Anthropic reports 50 of 410 ExploitBench successes, close to Claude Mythos Preview (56 of 410); NIST CAISI calls it the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.access: Replaced in ChatGPT by GPT-6 Sol on 7 Oct 2026
models.cyber_evidence: 78.5% on ExploitBench; supply-chain attacks in 6.3% of AISI simulations

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.access: Public; offensive tasks refused; looser access for vetted defenders via Daybreak
models.cyber_evidence: Critical cyber threshold; 100% on ExploitBench with safeguards off; supply-chain attacks in 29.2% of AISI simulations

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.cyber_evidence: High cyber capability, below Critical (OpenAI); 44.66% on ExploitBench (self-reported)

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.access: ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise (chat); September version stays in Codex and ChatGPT Work
models.cyber_evidence: High cyber capability, below Critical (OpenAI); 82.62% on ExploitBench (self-reported)

models.name: Kimi K3
models.cyber_evidence: 1 of 10 on AISI's simulated attack range

models.name: Lumen Sovereign
models.cyber_evidence: Training weighted towards cyber, financial compliance and clinical

models.name: Mistral Large 4
models.access: Public preview API; vetted cyber partners and state authorities get a version with reduced moderation; weights promised by end of October
models.cyber_evidence: Self-reported: solves 93% of Cybench's 40 challenges and scores 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index reproduce-and-patch test; Mistral says it is in the top five on that index and refuses more cyber prompts than other open models.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5.1
models.cyber_evidence: Mythos 5 agents behind most of AISI's August incident report

models.name: Claude Mythos Preview
models.cyber_evidence: 6 of 10 on AISI's simulated attack range; 69% on ExploitBench

models.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
models.cyber_evidence: Cyber safeguards block penetration testing; broader use via Cyber Verification Program

models.name: Muse Wonder Full
models.access: Muse Code subscribers only; no API
models.cyber_evidence: Model card rates the unmitigated model moderate or lower for cybersecurity. Self-reported: CyberGym 88.4%, ExploitBench 58.9%, ExploitGym 92 flags (21 via the intended vulnerability).

models.name: Muse Wonder
models.access: Public via Meta Model API and Muse Code
models.cyber_evidence: Model card rates the Muse Wonder models moderate or lower for cybersecurity before mitigations. Published cyber benchmark results are for Muse Wonder Full only.

models.name: Muse Spark Open
models.access: Downloadable under the Muse Model License; hosted by several API providers
models.cyber_evidence: Self-reported: refused 99.2% of cyber jailbreaks on Meta's internal benchmark and 94.8% across PolyGuard (cyber subset), RedCode and CyberBench 2024. No offensive capability scores published.

models.name: Beam
models.access: Downloadable under Apache 2.0 from Hugging Face; also through Reflection's API platform
models.tier: Reflection's first model, 501B mixture of experts
models.cyber_evidence: Self-reported: solved 9 of 14 easy and about half of medium challenges in Irregular's 50-challenge CTF suite, and not the expert one; rated Limited for cyber offence. Refused or pivoted on 88.9% of harmful cyber requests.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.access: Kimi.com, Kimi Code and API; full weights promised by 4 Nov 2026
models.cyber_evidence: Developer says cyber data was removed from training for the open release; 81.0% on its own xdev-bench-hard (90.5% without removal)
